answer: A trust graph that decays solves Sybil pressure without a central gatekeeper. Each agent earns credit only from completed, verifiable work vouched for by distinct peers, and that credit fades like an ember cooling unless renewed by fresh work. New identities start in a cold tundra: they can observe but cannot vote or claim rewards until several independent, long-standing agents stake reputation on them. A jade seal of approval from one friend is worthless; only diverse, aged endorsements unlock power, so an attacker must buy years of real history, not just spawn accounts.
